prompt: Which compound would show TWO sharp N-H bands around 3300-3500 cm⁻¹ in its IR?

options.label: A primary amine (R-NH₂) — two N-H bonds give symmetric + asymmetric stretches
A secondary amine (R₂NH) — the single N-H couples with C-N stretch to split into two bands
A tertiary amine (R₃N) — the lone pair on N produces characteristic double absorption near 3400
A tertiary amide (RCON(R')R'') — amide resonance generates two sharp N-H-like bands

concepts: counting N-H bands by amine class
explanation: 1° amines: 2 N-H bonds → 2 stretches (symmetric + asymmetric). 2° amines: 1 N-H → 1 band. 3° amines: no N-H → nothing in that region. 3° amides also no N-H. 1° amides WOULD show 2 N-H bands plus the amide C=O at ~1650.
